name: manual_1b1f21
claim: When work spans multiple repositories and multiple branches over an extended session, the coordination overhead is not optional bookkeeping -- it is what keeps concurrent, independent work (other agents, review bots, the user's own actions) from silently invalidating each other. Three concrete practices carried real weight this session: (1) a cross-linked status tracker in each repo's own docs/next/, so status lives next to the code it describes and points across the repo boundary rather than requiring institutional memory; (2) treating a stacked-branch relationship as a fact to reverify after any push to either end of the stack, not a one-time setup; (3) reconciling a stack with a plain merge rather than a rebase whenever the branch might already be visible elsewhere, since a merge is safe without extra authorization and a rebase is a history rewrite that can silently orphan another agent's or the user's already-fetched view of the branch.

decisions.notes: The coordination-overhead pattern that made cross-repo, cross-branch work resilient to concurrent, independent activity -- proven necessary, not just good practice.

rationale: The coordination-overhead pattern that made cross-repo, cross-branch work resilient to concurrent, independent activity -- proven necessary, not just good practice.
